f-first.exercise: Change either R or C and compare two transients at their 63% crossings.
f-first.evidence: Record the stimulus edge and both time constants on the same time axis.

f-connect.exercise: Use two unequal divider resistors, then disconnect the lower leg in a copy and use three probes to locate the open.
f-connect.evidence: Show where the voltage first disagrees with the divider calculation.

f-edit.exercise: Use Undo and Redo, then overlay the unchanged and edited transients.
f-edit.evidence: Measure each 63% crossing from its own input edge and identify the design revision of each trace.

f-hierarchy.exercise: Add a second divider instance and swap two ports on that instance alone.
f-hierarchy.evidence: Compare both outputs and name the parent-level pin mapping responsible for the error.

f-debug.exercise: Calculate the smallest load resistance that gives 0.89 V. Try a nearby standard resistor on either side of that boundary.
f-debug.evidence: Show the two measured voltages and why the voltage limit selects one resistor.

f-portfolio.exercise: Run Geometry DRC on an edited copy, then save, close and reopen it.
f-portfolio.evidence: Record one reported rule, its location and a geometry change to address it.

f-floating-voltage.exercise: Reverse the meter leads, or move both terminal voltages by the same amount.
f-floating-voltage.evidence: Show which change reverses the sign and which leaves the differential reading fixed.
distractors: The positive lead relative to ground, provided both nodes are above ground
The mean of the two lead voltages relative to ground

f-open-drain.exercise: Repeat on a 150 pF bus. Use the RC rise limit and the sink-current limit to narrow the possible pull-up values.
f-open-drain.evidence: Compare release time, low voltage and sink current for two nearby standard resistor values.
distractors: Current through the MOSFET body diode
The receiver input charging the bus from its logic supply

a-load.exercise: Try a second load value and compare it with the supplied loaded divider.
a-load.evidence: Record both equivalent lower-leg resistances and the measured terminal voltage.

a-bandwidth.exercise: Read the response at the corner and one decade beyond it. Compare a second capacitor value.
a-bandwidth.evidence: Report normalized gain, corner frequency, and the high-frequency slope.

a-bias.exercise: Sweep the output voltage over a range in a copy of the mirror fixture.
a-bias.evidence: Mark where current first leaves a 5% error band and compare with the width-ratio estimate.

a-differential.exercise: Run equal positive and negative differential inputs at fixed common mode.
a-differential.evidence: Compare the two branch currents, their sum, and the sign of the output change.

a-amplifier.exercise: Inspect device operating points and vary the output load in a copy.
a-amplifier.evidence: Name the high-impedance node and compare DC bias and measured low-frequency gain with your model.

a-layout.exercise: Move one matched unit off its symmetric location, keeping the schematic fixed.
a-layout.evidence: Compare centroid offset and route asymmetry. Identify which quantities came from geometry and which need extraction.

a-gmid-bias.exercise: Choose a second gate bias and compare the measured gm/ID to the square-law approximation at both biases.
a-gmid-bias.evidence: Record the two overdrives and explain why the expression is specific to the teaching model.

a-gmid-size.exercise: Try two nearby widths and keep the bias voltages fixed.
a-gmid-size.evidence: Show which satisfy the measured gm, drain-current and gm/ID tolerances.

a-gmid-headroom.exercise: Sweep the drain voltage through the compliance knee.
a-gmid-headroom.evidence: Find the lowest measured VDS meeting the stated headroom and current criteria.

a-gmid-tradeoff.exercise: Compare both bias choices with the same output load and frequency or transient stimulus.
a-gmid-tradeoff.evidence: Report width, current and measured speed separately. If the model omits important capacitance, state that limitation.

a-lc-bode.exercise: Change the damping resistance without changing L or C and inspect the low-pass and band-pass responses.
a-lc-bode.evidence: Record the resonant frequency, slope and phase reference, and explain what damping changed.

a-degeneration.exercise: Compare both matched-bias versions at a second sine amplitude.
a-degeneration.evidence: Report gain, current and distortion together and explain the trade-off.

a-rejection.exercise: Repeat differential, common-mode and supply excitations at another frequency.
a-rejection.evidence: Record input amplitudes, gains and rejection ratios separately. Keep rail feedthrough and input-referred PSRR distinct.

a-drive.exercise: Try a second compensation capacitor with the same command and both loads.
a-drive.evidence: Identify the worst load and compare final error, overshoot, current and settled-band time.

a-switch-drive.exercise: Repeat at an intermediate load resistance while keeping the gate within the supply.
a-switch-drive.evidence: Compare extracted on-resistance and voltage-drop margin with the original two loads.
distractors: Gate voltage relative to ground, even if the source moves
Drain-to-source voltage alone once the drain is pulled down

a-weak-sensor.exercise: Double the sensor source resistance or the capacitive load, one at a time.
a-weak-sensor.evidence: Identify which edit changes input error and which changes settling. Explain the limits of the functional buffer model.
distractors: Input resistance near the sensor resistance for a matched interface, with low output resistance
High input and high output resistance to isolate the two circuits

d-logic.exercise: Seed a single mux select mistake in a copy of the RTL.
d-logic.evidence: Give one input vector that catches it and check all eight vectors after the repair.

d-counter.exercise: Apply reset and enable on the same clock, then resume counting.
d-counter.evidence: Record the cycle table and show which event has priority and when wrap occurs.

d-pulse.exercise: Test a long request, then deassert and send the earliest legal second request.
d-pulse.evidence: Show exactly one pulse per accepted rising request and identify the rearm cycle.

d-pwm.exercise: Change duty midway through a period in a copy of the teaching bench.
d-pwm.evidence: Report the observed update policy and compare high-count at zero, midscale and maximum.

d-average.exercise: Use a set with a half-integer mean and insert a bubble in valid.
d-average.evidence: Calculate the worst-case sum width and show the rounded result and the exact ready cycle.

d-serial.exercise: Send an extra byte whose bit pattern differs from the supplied four cases.
d-serial.evidence: Mark start, data order, stop and busy on the waveform. Identify the simplified bit-clock assumption.

d-latch.exercise: Find the shortest select-and-data sequence that exposes the stale output.
d-latch.evidence: Show it failing on the starter and passing on the repair; name the assignment required for each select value.

d-saturation.exercise: Exercise a sum of exactly 15 followed by overflow and an invalid cycle.
d-saturation.evidence: Explain the carry bit, the saturated result and the hold behavior separately.

d-pipeline.exercise: Send consecutive valid words separated by one bubble and then reset.
d-pipeline.evidence: Use a cycle table to account for data, valid and the first permitted output after reset.

d-spi-register.exercise: Add a frame that aborts after a valid address and seven payload bits. Follow it with a valid read.
d-spi-register.evidence: Show both readbacks and mark MISO release and its allowed change edge.
distractors: Latch the write as soon as the eighth payload bit is sampled
Commit at chip-select rise whenever a valid command byte was received

m-bridge.exercise: Inspect an adjacent DAC trial near the decision for the original input.
m-bridge.evidence: Tie the DAC voltage, comparator bit and next RTL state to the same edge.

m-hold.exercise: Change the hold interval or load in a copy while keeping acquisition unchanged.
m-hold.evidence: Read the held-node voltage at the last comparison and express its error as a fraction of an LSB.

m-codes.exercise: Apply two values just below and above a nearby ideal code boundary.
m-codes.evidence: Report the two codes and signed quantization errors using the same reference and code convention.

m-settling.exercise: Try a different clock period that still meets the conversion deadline.
m-settling.evidence: Name the waveform that distinguishes inadequate acquisition from an RTL failure and record the first correct trial.

m-weight.exercise: Use a DAC code where only the repaired bit changes.
m-weight.evidence: Measure its effective weight and link it to an observed change at a code transition.

m-repeat.exercise: Test widely spaced starts and near-back-to-back legal starts.
m-repeat.evidence: Show one ordered completion per accepted start and explain how a busy-time request is treated.

m-ramp.exercise: Use a different ramp slope and keep uniform samples in time.
m-ramp.evidence: Compare one threshold estimate, the missing-code count and peak DNL and INL under a stated reference convention.

p-spec.exercise: Write the mirror brief so another student can set up its acceptance test without asking you for values.
p-spec.evidence: Include target, units, tolerance, supply and load conditions, and the exact quantity to measure.

p-review.exercise: Give a peer one saved project and its before-and-after evidence.
p-review.evidence: Have the peer reproduce the observation from the run references. Document one missing detail or limitation.

c-filter.exercise: Choose another input-filter value and run the acquisition tests at all eight samples.
c-filter.evidence: Compare the worst acquisition error and filter bandwidth. Show why the other two seeded faults do not explain this measurement.

c-sar.exercise: Run a different sequence of input levels in the integration fixture.
c-sar.evidence: Identify the earliest compare where the faulty design diverges and verify the corrected code order.

c-average.exercise: Use a block with a rounding tie and a separate block at maximum code.
c-average.evidence: Record bit growth, rounded values and the cycles where valid and alarm should change.

c-qualify.exercise: Take the first failing case in an intentionally altered copy and rerun it by itself.
c-qualify.evidence: Save the exact design, operating conditions and failing measurement so someone can reproduce it.

c-temperature.exercise: Inspect the worst held-out trial and repeat with a different input between calibration anchors.
c-temperature.evidence: Report gain and offset units, quantization contribution and the residual error after calibration.

l-width.exercise: Narrow a different route in a copy and use Geometry DRC to locate it.
l-width.evidence: Record the rule identifier, measured width and legal repair.

l-spacing.exercise: Choose a different legal placement within the same channel.
l-spacing.evidence: Calculate clearance from drawn edges and show the relevant spacing report.

l-via.exercise: Move the cut so it meets enclosure on one layer and misses on the other.
l-via.evidence: Read four margins on each layer and show that centering alone can miss a layer offset.

l-centroid.exercise: Compare ABBA and BAAB under a simple linear and quadratic gradient.
l-centroid.evidence: Compute the locations of both group centers and explain the residual the layout does not cancel.

l-layout-decisions.exercise: Choose an additional route width or layer stack after the overview.
l-layout-decisions.evidence: Keep the endpoints fixed and compare connectivity, resistance estimate and measured bandwidth.

l-fold.exercise: Compare one and four fingers at fixed device width. Zoom in to count diffusion and contacts.
l-fold.evidence: Show what the PDK means by total width and report one layout quantity that changes.

l-body.exercise: Leave an intentional open on the body branch in a copy.
l-body.evidence: Name the body net and correct rail. Compare the process verification reports around the repair.

l-match.exercise: Add one longer access route to a copy of the matched layout.
l-match.evidence: Compare the two centroids and route asymmetry, then explain which error could remain under a systematic gradient.

l-dac.exercise: Try a different stub route with all capacitor tiles in place.
l-dac.evidence: Show which code transitions move and compare endpoint INL under the same model.

l-lvs.exercise: Diagnose one seeded fault without looking at its name.
l-lvs.evidence: Identify the first discrepant port or net using terminal connectivity, and compare this evidence with process LVS in the inverter world.

l-eco.exercise: Inspect both parent instances after changing the shared child. Undo and redo one revision.
l-eco.evidence: Record the affected routes and confirm an unchanged port mapping at both instances.

l-settle.exercise: Compare two stub or routing changes with the same differential pair.
l-settle.evidence: Measure differential settling error at the same deadline and report which parasitics the fixture models.

l-noise.exercise: Compare same-layer spacing with the shield or alternate-layer fixture.
l-noise.evidence: Explain which coupling path the teaching model can compute and what an independent field model would need.

l-supply.exercise: Try a second width near the minimum and keep the load fixed.
l-supply.evidence: Calculate drop from sheet resistance and compare the two values with the allowed supply drop.

l-floorplan.exercise: Save two placements that preserve the obstacle and pin access.
l-floorplan.evidence: Compare area, inter-port routing distance and one constraint that changes the ranking.

l-access.exercise: Compare the compact macro’s Metal 1 route and a two-layer alternative.
l-access.evidence: Report both lengths, via counts and the terminal connectivity from the same port pair.

l-pad-ring.exercise: Swap two signal pad assignments in a copy and trace them back to the core.
l-pad-ring.evidence: Name the mismatch using the intended pin map and show the repaired landing.

l-density.exercise: Compare two fill keepouts that obey the required density windows.
l-density.evidence: Record worst coverage and added loading under the fixture’s teaching coefficients.

l-antenna.exercise: Compare the jumper and diode on the same antenna fault.
l-antenna.evidence: Report the early metal ratio, any added load and the model assumptions about layer order.

l-via-current.exercise: Compare the smallest crossing array that meets the current limit with one larger array.
l-via-current.evidence: Record equal-share current per cut and measured path drop. Explain what this model omits about current crowding.

l-isolation.exercise: Open a guard segment or reroute it to a noisy return in a copy.
l-isolation.evidence: Show the continuity failure and identify which substrate coupling mechanism the physical inspection cannot measure.

l-spiral.exercise: Compare two feasible coil geometries by changing just one dimension.
l-spiral.evidence: Report L, Q, and self-resonance under the same model. State which comparison would benefit from EM extraction.

l-handoff.exercise: Give the exported GDS to a peer and assign a different pin label fault in a copy.
l-handoff.evidence: Identify the actual top, pin-purpose layer and label location from the written file.

l-mim-plate.exercise: Compare two routes with the capacitor body and pin assignments fixed.
l-mim-plate.evidence: Estimate the area/perimeter change and compare the resulting added ground capacitance.
distractors: The total access-metal area, with permission to swap the two plate nets
The access route’s turn count, with permission to change the active area

l-decoupling.exercise: Keep the same capacitor and compare a second placement or pulse width.
l-decoupling.evidence: Record the resistance of both loop branches and the corresponding load droop. State the model’s limits.
distractors: Only the resistance from the external source to the load matters
Only the DC voltage at the external supply matters

project-opamp.exercise: Hold bias current fixed and compare two compensation candidates at the same load.
project-opamp.evidence: Record first unity crossing, phase margin, DC current and a transient criterion with the named fixture.

project-tia.exercise: Try a second photodiode capacitance while retaining the feedback network.
project-tia.evidence: Report signed transimpedance, corner frequency and settling. Explain the dominant feedback limitation.

project-miller.exercise: Keep 2 pF compensation and compare 500 Ω, 1 kΩ and 2 kΩ, then change the load.
project-miller.evidence: Save first unity frequency, phase margin and zero location. Explain the effect of changing load.

project-ahuja.exercise: Compare a 10 MHz and 50 MHz buffer pole at two output loads.
project-ahuja.evidence: Save the first unity crossing and phase margin for each case. Explain what the ideal model leaves out.

project-bias-reference.exercise: Move the output clamp to a neighboring voltage with the same RSET.
project-bias-reference.evidence: Compare output current to the reference current and report the direction of compliance error.

project-cascode.exercise: Find the limiting transistor at the compliance boundary before and after cascode sizing.
project-cascode.evidence: Compare measured and estimated headroom and identify the worst tested PVT case.

project-bandgap-widlar.exercise: Sweep the trim resistor around the passing choice and compare the two startup ramps.
project-bandgap-widlar.evidence: Explain the PTAT and CTAT contributions, trim sensitivity and worst startup case.

project-bandgap-brokaw.exercise: Change the trim and inspect how the current-density ratio contributes to VREF.
project-bandgap-brokaw.evidence: Record a ΔVBE estimate, measured temperature variation and startup at one held-out case.

project-bandgap-kuijk.exercise: Compare the Kuijk and Brokaw branch relationships using the same operating conditions.
project-bandgap-kuijk.evidence: Identify how each feedback loop sets branch currents and explain one startup difference.

project-bandgap-banba.exercise: Sweep supply from the nominal fixture in a copy while keeping the trim fixed.
project-bandgap-banba.evidence: Separate the low output reference from the required supply and report the first lost condition.

interview-differential.exercise: Drive the pair with balanced inputs and repeat the supplied single-sided sweep.
interview-differential.evidence: Compare steering at equal differential input. Identify the common-mode shift in the single-sided case.

interview-input-pairs.exercise: Check one extra common-mode voltage near each topology’s measured limit.
interview-input-pairs.evidence: Compare branch current and gain, and name the device with limiting headroom.

interview-gain.exercise: Read closely spaced points on two current sweeps to estimate gm and ro.
interview-gain.evidence: Show the finite differences and units, then compare gain near and away from the knee.

interview-slew.exercise: Compare a second load and fit the linear portion of the output ramp.
interview-slew.evidence: Report slew and settled-band time separately, and compare the slope with the I/C estimate.

interview-noise.exercise: Change source resistance again or choose a different integration band.
interview-noise.evidence: Separate noise density from RMS and identify which contributor changes the budget.

interview-mismatch.exercise: Hold the original seed fixed during sizing and then run a second seed.
interview-mismatch.evidence: Report mean, sample standard deviation and sample count, and explain why the observed pass fraction is uncertain.

interview-comparator.exercise: Test the opposite sign or a smaller magnitude of input overdrive.
interview-comparator.evidence: Report decision time and kickback separately and connect delay to regenerative gain.

interview-sar.exercise: Try a second input or acquisition interval after the capacitor repair.
interview-sar.evidence: Compare the charge-ratio estimate, hold pedestal and resulting code in the same fixture.

interview-ldo.exercise: Run a new load-step or ESR condition with dropout and supply held fixed.
interview-ldo.evidence: Show measured droop and time in the 2% band. Identify which measurement supports a stability claim.

interview-post-layout-debug.exercise: Find two widths close to the passing limit under the same routing condition.
interview-post-layout-debug.evidence: Report the smallest passing width, 50 ps error and added modeled capacitance.

project-chopper.exercise: Repeat at an additional input level or try a small demodulator phase offset.
project-chopper.evidence: Compare measured gain, offset, ripple and settling using consistent averaging windows.

project-relaxation.exercise: Change the timing capacitance and inspect four late cycles after the startup pulse.
project-relaxation.evidence: Compare the period estimate with measured frequency, duty and startup delay.

project-pll.exercise: Try a smaller filter time constant near critical damping and compare both step directions.
project-pll.evidence: Report the filter values, measured overshoot, entry into the 2 Hz band and late phase drift for both directions.

project-pga.exercise: Choose a second selector sequence in a copy of the switching fixture.
project-pga.evidence: Report per-code gain and bandwidth and the worst transition. State the AC switch approximation.

project-window-detector.exercise: Try another bounded noise amplitude near the threshold.
project-window-detector.evidence: Count extra transitions and measure both cutoff errors separately.
distractors: Above the lower bound or below the upper bound
Outside the band, when only one comparator condition is true

project-swcap-gain.exercise: Change sample amplitude or clock rate in a copy while holding the capacitor ratio fixed.
project-swcap-gain.evidence: Show plate voltages in both phases and compare gain, deadline error and hold droop.
distractors: Feedback capacitance divided by sampling capacitance
Sampling capacitance divided by the sum of feedback and output-load capacitance

project-tunable-gmc.exercise: Try a midpoint tuning voltage with the same capacitor.
project-tunable-gmc.evidence: Compare cutoff with gm/(2πC) and check gain and THD. State which behavior depends on the OTA model.
distractors: Increasing capacitance at the same bias
Increasing signal amplitude while holding the small-signal bias fixed

tb-divider-bias.exercise: Install an unequal divider ratio in a copy and build the same operating-point measurement.
tb-divider-bias.evidence: Show the calculated and measured node voltage and identify the positive and reference nodes.

tb-divider-sweep.exercise: Use a shorter sweep span and extract endpoints and slope.
tb-divider-sweep.evidence: Keep the same source and units in both editors, and compare the fitted gain.

tb-divider-transient.exercise: Double the load capacitor in a copy.
tb-divider-transient.evidence: Measure the 63% crossing from the edge and compare the final amplitude and Thevenin time constant.

tb-tia-bias.exercise: Add a no-photocurrent run and a second nonzero bias point.
tb-tia-bias.evidence: Show signed output change per ampere and check how it relates to the resistor.

tb-tia-ac.exercise: Sample a second frequency or change photocurrent AC amplitude.
tb-tia-ac.evidence: Report both output voltage and normalized transimpedance. State when the small-signal result applies.

tb-tia-step.exercise: Compare an extra photodiode or load capacitance at the same step current.
tb-tia-step.evidence: Report final value, worst undershoot and time last entering the band.

tb-opamp-bias.exercise: Measure input error and supply or bias current along with output voltage.
tb-opamp-bias.evidence: Document whether the operating point meets both output and current conditions.

tb-opamp-ac.exercise: Inspect the loop fixture at DC and at midband, then examine its first falling unity crossing.
tb-opamp-ac.evidence: Record the phase at that same crossing and distinguish the loop result from one gain sample.

tb-opamp-step.exercise: Compare the same follower with a second capacitive load.
tb-opamp-step.evidence: Report first edge time, overshoot and the final entry into the settling band. Keep the late reading for reference.

tb-balanced-stimulus.exercise: Delay one edge in an edited copy to create a short common-mode step.
tb-balanced-stimulus.evidence: Plot or tabulate differential and common-mode voltage through the transition and show both workflows report the same failure.
distractors: Drive one input to 1.00 V and hold the other at 0.90 V
Drive the inputs to 1.00 V and 0.80 V

sc-inv.exercise: Trace one pull-up and one pull-down path in the physical layout, then inspect the effect of opening one path in a copy.
sc-inv.evidence: Show the contact or route that isolates the failing vector.

sc-nand2.exercise: Compare both orders of the two input transitions at the same load.
sc-nand2.evidence: Trace the internal stack node and record the two measured falling delays.

sc-nor2.exercise: Run a loaded pull-up transition and compare it with the analogous NAND path.
sc-nor2.evidence: Explain the series PMOS path and show what sets the slower transition.

sc-aoi21.exercise: Toggle C once with A and B held, then choose a separate A/B route to exercise.
sc-aoi21.evidence: Show which transistor path controls Y for each vector and its expected Boolean result.

sc-mux2.exercise: Inspect SELECTED and Y for a data edge and a select edge with the same output level.
sc-mux2.evidence: Trace the complementary switches and separate the internal level from the buffered output.

sc-dff.exercise: Move D during the noncapturing clock phase and inspect both latch stages.
sc-dff.evidence: Show the next Q change and the interval in which Q retains its old value.

sc-inv-compact.exercise: Try a neighboring pitch while preserving the row and power tracks.
sc-inv-compact.evidence: Record horizontal width and verify both rail connections and the same logic.

sc-nand-drive.exercise: Measure a second input arc or load after meeting the 40 fF target.
sc-nand-drive.evidence: Compare delay with the original stack and describe the input-loading cost of wider transistors.

sc-dff-clock.exercise: Compare two driver splits with similar total width.
sc-dff-clock.evidence: Record both clock-to-Q delays and explain the different rise and fall sensitivities.

sc-abutment.exercise: Insert a small vertical offset or gap into a copy of the passing row.
sc-abutment.evidence: Show the first seam or continuity error and identify the intended rail connection.

sc-nor-rise.exercise: Check the same revised PMOS width at a second fixture load.
sc-nor-rise.evidence: Report delay improvement and total input-gate width in addition to cell footprint.

sc-nand-input.exercise: Integrate the driving current around a second vector transition.
sc-nand-input.evidence: Compare effective switched capacitance and loaded delay using the declared current direction.

sc-mux-glitch.exercise: Change the explicit coupling stress or select slew in a copy.
sc-mux-glitch.evidence: Read glitch peak and time outside an error band at each settled logic level.

sc-buffer-fo4.exercise: Compare two stage ratios under the same total width and four loads.
sc-buffer-fo4.evidence: Report both delays and show which stage limits the poorer design.

sc-xor-energy.exercise: Test another legal one-bit transition sequence.
sc-xor-energy.evidence: Declare the current integral and number of transitions, then compare energy and worst delay.

sc-dff-aperture.exercise: Choose the nearest passing row and adjacent failing row for both sweeps. Repeat with opposite data polarity in a copy.
sc-dff-aperture.evidence: Record both brackets, their resolution and whether Q capture or delay set each limit.

sc-half-adder.exercise: Compare the shared NAND construction with an independent carry path under the same row assumptions.
sc-half-adder.evidence: Save both truth tables, width and the slowest arc for each output.
distractors: The uncomplemented product A AND B directly in both NAND sum branches
The complement of A OR B reused as the carry term

sc-schmitt.exercise: Add bounded ripple to a slow rising and falling input in a copy.
sc-schmitt.evidence: Read the two thresholds and count extra output crossings at the specified noise amplitude.
distractors: A at the two supply half-level input crossings
Y measured once with the input low and once with it high

sc-tristate.exercise: Overlap the two driver enables in a copy and compare against break-before-make.
sc-tristate.evidence: Report branch current during the overlap, released-bus current and actual handoff timing separately.
distractors: To read propagation delay while both drivers are enabled
To establish valid logic without checking whether the disabled output is fighting the bias

inverter-process.exercise: Inspect a second available PDK profile and locate its device binding and nominal teaching voltage.
inverter-process.evidence: Name the two revisions and their available models, layout generators and verification tools.

inverter-schematic.exercise: Seed one incorrect body connection in a copy.
inverter-schematic.evidence: Trace the four required terminals and identify why the modified topology violates the intended body connection.

inverter-dc.exercise: Estimate VIL and VIH by marking where the local transfer slope reaches −1.
inverter-dc.evidence: Show both noise margins and identify the difference between VM and the input limits.

inverter-transient.exercise: Repeat at another output load, then repeat with a finer output time step.
inverter-transient.evidence: Report tPHL and tPLH separately from rise and fall slew and compare numerical consistency.

inverter-layout.exercise: Inspect the process layers at all four terminal contacts.
inverter-layout.evidence: Annotate one route from gate, drain, source and body to its named pin or rail.

inverter-drc.exercise: Seed a second process-rule violation in a copy and run the matching deck.
inverter-drc.evidence: Save the rule ID, measured dimension, location and evidence of repair.

inverter-lvs.exercise: Run extraction on a copy with a deliberately disconnected terminal.
inverter-lvs.evidence: Identify the first mismatched device or net and compare the repaired and faulty reports.

inverter-handoff.exercise: Build a manifest for the final design and ask a peer to reproduce one test.
inverter-handoff.evidence: Tie bias, delay, DRC and LVS to exact revisions and named conditions and state one remaining test.
